analysis.title: GS Basics: China Restrictions. 2018 Playbook. FCI Tight.
key_insights: US equities liquidated sharply from the open on 11/19. SPX reversed 3.3% intraday, took out virtually every reasonable support area, and closed at a bearish high/low close. Only 38 S&P constituents advanced and 464 declined.

New BIS chip export rules, effective November 19 and directed by Treasury and the NSC, tighten restrictions on direct chip sales to China and on advanced compute accessed remotely by Chinese entities through overseas data centers. The author reads it as an attempt to close the offshore compute loophole, with substantial overlap with the proposed RASA legislation.

China faces pressure on three fronts: direct access to advanced chips, remote access to overseas compute, and the ability to manufacture leading-edge technology, with tighter restrictions on overseas foundries.

The author sees the most immediate issue as uncertainty over who can access what under which licensing regime, which may freeze incremental investment decisions, rather than permanent loss of Chinese demand. This partly explains the weak Asian data center trade alongside broader China weakness and Shanghai testing its lows.

Four factors the author cites as driving multiples down: cost of capital (further challenged by a change of leadership at NVDA), data center restrictions, oversupply and efficiency unlocks for inference, and lack of revenue to support capex.

The defensive bid failed. Utilities and staples sold off with everything else despite lower Treasury yields. They outperformed relatively but gave no protection in absolute terms. The author says the rolling rotation increasingly looks like outright equity liquidation.
Negative gamma into expiry likely amplified the equity move.

Financial conditions have tightened very quickly. Waller's 50bp comments helped shock the market, and Fed speakers this week were mostly hawkish. The author sees November/December 2018 parallels as increasingly close and says the Fed risks overtightening into a market already under stress.

2yr inflation breakevens have collapsed toward their lows while 2yr real yields sit near relative highs, a large tightening in real policy conditions. The long end may be pricing a policy mistake, with yields and breakevens falling while equities and gold liquidate.
The author says the market pivots when central banks pivot. Receiving rates and owning duration is the trade that looks most misaligned with equity internals and remains relatively attractive.
Gold is flagged as a coincidental indicator to watch alongside equities. It is liquidating in reaction to real rates and FCI.

From a contrarian positioning view, the depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest the market may be approaching a tactical local low. The author notes few catalysts ahead: PCE next Wednesday, NFP and the December FOMC, with November CPI the next major anchor.
